messages.content: today was just a day. i worked, ate dinner, and came home. i do not have a big story.
you do not need a big story to talk. was there any small part you would like to tell me about, or would you rather keep it simple?
i liked the walk home. the air was cold, but i was warm enough.
that sounds like a part you could enjoy without the whole day having to be different.
i do not want to call it the best part. it was just nice.
then nice is enough. you had a walk home that you liked.
can you write about my day without making up feelings?
i worked, ate dinner, and came home. i liked the walk home. the air was cold, but i was warm enough.
why did you not say i was lonely when i walked?
you did not say you were lonely. being on a walk and feeling lonely are different things. i should not add a feeling you did not give.
what if i tell you now that i was walking with my sister?
then i can put her in the part about the walk. that gives who was there, but it still does not tell me every feeling you had.
write only that part now.
i liked walking home with my sister. the air was cold, but i was warm enough.
if i tell you an animal is near the door, can you know which animal it is?
no. animal is a general word. it does not tell me which animal you mean unless you give more information.
what if i say it is the same animal i told you about before?
if that information is in our conversation, i can use it. if i do not have that information, i should ask rather than choose an animal myself.
can i give it a name to help us talk about the same one?
yes. a name can help us know which animal you mean when we talk about it again. the name alone does not tell us everything about the animal.
what facts could i give without using a more specific animal word?
you could tell me its size, where it is, what it is doing, or other details you know. those facts can help answer questions about it even when you use the general word animal.
i say the animal is small and sleeping near the door. is it hungry?
we do not know. small and sleeping do not tell us for sure whether it is hungry.
is it near the door?
yes, from the information you gave.
can you explain why one answer is sure and the other is not?
you gave the place as a fact, so i can use that. you did not give information about whether it is hungry, so i should leave that question open.
write a story about a person thinking someone moved their cup because they did not care about it. the real reason should be simple.

a woman left her cup on a table before going to answer the phone. when she came back, the cup was on a shelf. she thought her brother had moved it because he did not want her things on the table. she asked him why he had put it there. he said that he needed to carry a large container through the room and was worried that the cup might break. now that the container was in the kitchen, he could put the cup back. she had seen the change, but had not known the reason for it.
what did she know before asking?
she knew the cup was in a different place. she did not know why her brother had moved it.
was her feeling the same as knowing his reason?
no. she had an idea about his reason, but that idea was not a fact she had checked.
what question could she use without saying he was wrong?
why did you move my cup to the shelf?
make his answer short.
i needed to carry something through here and did not want to break your cup.
can she still ask him to tell her next time?
yes. she can understand his reason and still ask for a message next time. she could say: thanks for taking care of it. please tell me when you move it so i know where to look.
finish the story with that request.
she said thank you for taking care of the cup and asked him to tell her next time he moved it. he put it back on the table, where she could reach it.
give me a simple example with some water and one with any water.
there is some water in the cup. is there any water in the cup?
can i use some in a question?
yes. would you like some water is a useful question when you are asking whether someone wants water.
so is it wrong to say any in every question?

no. is there any water asks whether water is there at all. would you like some water asks whether someone wants water you can give them. we use the question and context to understand which meaning is needed.
i have water on the table and want to ask my friend whether they want it. what should i say?
would you like some water?
now ask whether the empty looking cup has water inside.
is there any water in the cup?
what if i know it has no water and want to say that?
there is no water in the cup.
can you give a small conversation using those ideas?
is there any water in the cup? no, the cup is empty. would you like some water? yes, please.
why did you not say yes to the empty cup question?
because you said the cup has no water. the reply should keep that fact, even though someone can put water in it later.
my note says i put the book on the table and moved it near the window. what did i move?
it could mean the book or the table. the word it does not make that choice clear enough by itself.
i moved the table. write the note clearly.
i put the book on the table and moved the table near the window.
that has table again. is using the same word again always wrong?
no. using the same word again can help when it makes the meaning clear. using it instead of a word such as it can help the person reading understand what you mean.
can you make it clear with two sentences?
i put the book on the table. then i moved the table near the window.
now make it about moving only the book.
i put the book on the table. then i moved the book near the window.
does that tell us whether the book is still on the table?
not for sure. it could be on a part of the table near the window, or in a different place. you would need to say more if that detail is important.
it is on the shelf near the window. put that in the note.
i put the book on the table. then i moved it to the shelf near the window.
why is it more clear now?
the book is put on the table in the first sentence and moved to the shelf in the next. saying to the shelf gives the new place clearly.
i have ten free minutes. i do not want to make a big plan. i just want to choose between reading and drawing.
which feels more like what you want right now: getting into a story, or making something on a page?
making something, but i do not know what to draw.
you could start with one thing you can see, such as your cup or the window. it does not need to become a full picture in ten minutes.
i do not want to draw what i see. i want something made up.
then you could draw a room you would like to sit in. you can choose its shape and what goes inside. it does not need to be a real place.
that sounds nice. do not give me a list of things for the room.
okay. you can let the first line on the page lead to the next one.
what if ten minutes is not enough to finish?
you can stop with a drawing that is still growing. finishing the picture is a different goal from having a few minutes to enjoy drawing.
can you say that more simply?
you can enjoy drawing for ten minutes without finishing the picture.
thanks. i am going to try it.
i hope you enjoy the time with your page.
write a story about someone answering a note before reading the last line.

a boy found a note from his sister asking whether he wanted to go to the park. he began writing yes on the back before reading the rest. the last line said that she wanted to go tomorrow morning, when he would be at school. he stopped and read the whole note again. then he wrote that he would like to go, but could only come in the afternoon. when his sister came home, they chose a time that worked for both of them.
what did his first answer leave out?
he had not thought about the time. yes to the idea of going was not the same as yes to tomorrow morning.
was the first part of the note false?
no. the later line added an important detail. the first part was not the whole request.
write his answer as a message to his sister.
i would like to go to the park, but i will be at school tomorrow morning. could we go in the afternoon instead?
what if she needs to go in the morning?
then they may need a different day, or she may go without him. they need a time when both are free if they want to go together.
say that last part more simply.
they need a time when both are free if they want to go together.
now end with a different day chosen.
his sister could not go in the afternoon, so they chose another day when both were free. he put the note away after reading every line.
what is the difference between who is at the door and whose key is this?
who is at the door asks which person is there. whose key is this asks which person has the key as their own.
give an answer to each.
my brother is at the door. this key is mine.
can the key be mine even if my brother is holding it?
yes. holding something does not always mean that it is yours. your brother could be holding your key for you.
make a sentence that says both things.
my brother is holding my key.
now ask about the person holding it.
who is holding my key?
now ask about the key, without saying it is mine.
whose key is my brother holding?
why does the question change?
the first question asks for the person who is holding the key. the other asks whose key it is, while already saying that your brother is holding it.
can the answer to the last question be mine?
yes. mine is a short answer to whose key is my brother holding.
